title: CLI reference
description: Use smu to discover modules, inspect a blueprint, apply changes, and maintain an installed setup.

sections.title: Common commands
paragraphs: Run smu --help on the installed machine for the available flags. The table groups frequently used commands by task.

Commands with output such as status, plan, or diff are useful before applying a change. Use the bundled Python CLI from Quick start when you need to target a specific checkout or want to avoid setup work performed by the legacy shell wrapper.
table: List available modules for the host.
Preview module changes for the named module.

sections.title: Target the intended checkout
paragraphs: The Python CLI uses SMU_HOME_DIR, or $HOME/set-me-up if it is unset, to find the blueprint. Keep the variable set when running from a non-default directory. Check which smu your shell resolves if the command appears to read a different setup.

sections.title: Inspect or manage rcm symlinks
paragraphs: With rcm installed, use --lsrc to list files that would be symlinked, --rcup to link them, or --rcdn to remove links.
Review the source and destination paths from --lsrc. The apply and removal flags change symlinks, so use them after checking that the dotfiles directory points at the intended checkout.

sections.title: Use structured output
paragraphs: Use --json on commands that support it to collect structured status and preflight data. Check the installed version’s help before depending on a flag in automation.

A JSON report can describe a failure even when it is valid JSON. Check the exit status and report-specific fields before running dependent commands. In adapter preflight, inspect can_apply and errors. For status, read the modules list and retain unknown as a separate state.
sections.code:
smu status --json
smu provisioning-adapter preflight --adapter rcm --profile default --json
